title: Pōhaku Tumble: Hawaiian term verification

conventions.kahako: precomposed vowels with macron (U+0101 ā, U+0113 ē, U+012B ī, U+014D ō, U+016B ū; capitals U+0100, U+0112, U+012A, U+014C, U+016A), text NFC-normalised
conventions.note: Several sources type U+2018 or an apostrophe for the ʻokina. Spellings below are re-keyed with U+02BB.

not_consulted: Pukui & Elbert (wehewehe.org and its mirrors), puke.ulukau.org, trussel2.com and the en.wiktionary API were deliberately not accessed. Pukui-Elbert readings appear only where a reachable source quotes or cites them.

terms.meaning: 32 houses, each 11.25° wide; 4 of them are the cardinal points, 7 named houses fill each quadrant (4 × 7 + 4 = 32).
terms.notes: Each name marks the centre of its house, so a house spans ±5.625° around its point. The house names are modern: the PVS archive says they "were devised by Nainoa Thompson" (it credits Will Kyselka, An Ocean in Mind, pp. 96-97). The cardinal and quadrant (wind) names are older Hawaiian words. Present the houses as the PVS / Nainoa Thompson star compass, not as ancient names.

terms.proposed: order Lā, ʻĀina, Noio, Manu, Nā Lani, Nā Leo, Haka (east toward north), repeated in each quadrant
terms.spelling: Lā, ʻĀina, Noio, Manu, Nālani, Nā Leo, Haka
terms.meaning: Lā is next to Hikina/Komohana and Haka is next to ʻĀkau/Hema in every quadrant.
terms.notes: The order is mirrored, not rotated. It always runs from the E or W point toward the N or S point. Going clockwise from north you get Haka, Nā Leo, Nālani, Manu, Noio, ʻĀina, Lā (NE), then Hikina, then Lā, ʻĀina, Noio, Manu, Nālani, Nā Leo, Haka (SE), and so on. Code that rotates one 7-name list by 90° per quadrant puts SE and NW in the wrong order. See the 32-house table.

terms.proposed: a star rising in a house in the east sets in the house of the same name in the west
terms.meaning: A star that rises in house X in Koʻolau (NE) sets in house X in Hoʻolua (NW). A star that rises in X in Malanai (SE) sets in X in Kona (SW).
terms.notes: The rule holds. The quadrant mirrors north-south (NE→NW, SE→SW) and a star never crosses from the north half to the south half. Do not confuse it with swells and wind: those cross the compass to the same house name in the diagonally opposite quadrant (Manu Koʻolau → Manu Kona), 180° away.

alternatives_and_doubts.detail: PVS diagram, archive, 1992 release, hokulea.com and the 2021 UH dissertation all write it as one word (Nālani / Nalani). Karjala (2019 UH thesis) writes "nā lani".
Two words in the PVS diagram, the archive, the 1992 release and the UH dissertation. "Nāleo" (one word) in current hokulea.com prose. "NaLeo" once in the archive star-line tables.
Devised by Nainoa Thompson (PVS archive, citing Kyselka, An Ocean in Mind, pp. 96-97). The cardinal and quadrant names are older Hawaiian words; the quadrant assignment is a PVS convention.
The Micronesian compass Thompson's system is based on. Its 32 points are named for the stars that rise and set there (rising = Tan, setting = Tupul). It is a different system, not a variant spelling.

alternatives_and_doubts.item: Wind meanings behind the quadrant names
alternatives_and_doubts.detail: Andrews calls Malanai a name of the gentle NE trade wind and Hoʻolua the strong north wind. Pukui-Elbert (cited by PVS) gives Kiu as the NW wind. The quadrant names are PVS labels, not literal wind bearings.
Sharatan and Hamal are listed as "'Aina-Koʻolau and La-Hoʻolua", which contradicts the same-house rule. These are transcription slips; the rule is stated plainly on the same site.
